newsitem.title: CANADA: Some Alberta Safeway workers vote to end strike.
newsitem.headline: Some Alberta Safeway workers vote to end strike.

text.p: Striking Canada Safeway Ltd employees in Calgary voted narrowly late on Wednesday to accept a mediated settlement that would end an often bitter 72-day-old walkout.
The rest of the grocery chain's 10,000 employees across Alberta were scheduled to vote on the proposal through June 10, starting on Thursday with staff in Edmonton.
Officials with the United Food and Commercial Workers union said the picket lines in front of Calgary Safeway stores would remain until Edmonton employees voted.
The Calgary Herald newspaper reported that of the 1,601 ballots cast in Wednesday's Calgary vote, 941 or 58.7 percent favored the mediated deal.
Canada Safeway, a unit of Pleasanton, Calif.-based Safeway Inc, and its Alberta unions went back to the bargaining table on May 28 with a mediator.
The mediator on Wednesday recommended a basis for settlement that did not address all oustanding issues in the dispute.
The chain's Alberta grocery clerks, cashiers and meat cutters, who have been without a labor contract since early last year, walked off the job on March 25.
Union negotiators have attempted to regain wage cuts the employees took in 1993 as well as increase working hours and wages for part-time employees.
The company has said its pay structure must be in line with its competitors in the province.
